items.title: Wallstedt living 'the dream' after emerging for Wild
items.summary:
Jesper Wallstedt still remembers.
Late nights, or perhaps early mornings depending on the schedule, parked next to his brother with a chance to tune into a New York Rangers game.
More specifically, a Henrik Lundqvist start.
items.body: Swedish goaltender continuing success from last season with countryman Gustavsson injured Late nights, or perhaps early mornings depending on the schedule, parked next to his brother with a chance to tune into a New York Rangers game. items.title: Cuthbert says winning Foster Hewitt Award 'ultimate honor'
items.summary: Chris Cuthbert grew up listening to Foster Hewitt and never imagined he would one day be receiving the Hockey Hall of Fame media award named after the legendary Canadian broadcaster.
items.body: Broadcasting icon's legendary calls include 'Golden Goal' for Canada at 2010 Olympics Chris Cuthbert grew up listening to Foster Hewitt and never imagined he would one day be receiving the Hockey Hall of Fame media award named after the legendary Canadian broadcaster. Cuthbert, this year's recipient of the Foster Hewitt Memorial Award for his outstanding contribution to broadcasting, will be honored at the Hockey Hall of Fame media luncheon in Toronto on Nov. 9. "It's overwhelming and it's the ultimate honor for an NHL broadcaster for sure," the 69-year-old told NHL.com. "I may be one of the last of the recipients who grew up listening to Foster Hewitt. He was the first guy to set the dream in motion. I'd go to bed at night with Foster Hewitt on the radio under the pillow listening to him." Cuthbert has become a Canadian broadcasting icon in his own right as the play-by-play voice for a generation of hockey fans. His call of Sidney Crosby 's overtime winner against the United States at the 2010 Vancouver Olympics has been compared to that of Hewitt's in Game 8 of the 1972 Summit Series when Paul Henderson scored the winning goal for Canada against the Soviet Union. Cuthbert was 15 when Hewitt famously exclaimed, "Here's a shot, Henderson made a wild stab for it and fell. Here's another shot, right in front, they score! Henderson has scored for Canada!" More than 37 years later, Cuthbert had a famous line of his own: "Crosby scores! Sidney Crosby, the golden goal and Canada has a once-in-a-lifetime Olympic gold!" Like Hewitt's famous call, Canadian hockey fans remember where they were listening to Cuthbert in the gold medal final. He has been eligible to sign a new deal since July 1 and can become an unrestricted free agent after the season. The 33-year-old forward became the Lightning’s all-time leading scorer on Saturday with an assist in a 5-4 overtime loss at the Utah Mammoth to pass Steven Stamkos (1,137). He has 15 points (four goals, 11 assists) in 12 games this season for the Lightning (8-3-1). Before the season, BriseBois sounded confident the sides could eventually reach a new deal. items.title: Reeling Jets fall to Panthers for eighth straight loss
items.body: SUNRISE, Fla. — Anton Lundell had a hat trick, Seth Jones capped a record-setting month with a goal and two assists, and the Florida Panthers topped the reeling Winnipeg Jets 5-2 on Friday night for their sixth win in eight games. Jones finished October with 18 points — two goals and 16 assists — to break the record for most points by a Florida defenseman in any month. Keith Yandle had 17 points for the Panthers in March 2018. Kyle Connor had his team-best 11th goal for Winnipeg, which dropped both ends of a home-and-home with Florida this week and is winless in its last eight games — going 0-6-2 in that span. Morgan Barron had his first goal of the season midway through the third to get the Jets to 3-2, but Lundell's second of the night restored Florida's two-goal edge. Lundell finished off the hat trick — Florida's fifth already this season — with an empty-netter with 1:39 left. Akira Schmid stopped 22 shots for Florida, which remains without standout forwards Aleksander Barkov and Brad Marchand because of injuries. Both resumed skating this week; Marchand could be back in about three weeks and Barkov in about four, Panthers coach Paul Maurice said. Florida's Bokondji Imama and Winnipeg's Tyrel Bauer brawled just 2:04 into the game, a reenactment of sorts of their still-talked-about fight in the AHL in 2024. They went at it for more than a minute Friday and — similar to what happened at the end of their fight two years ago — shared a respectful nod toward the other when it was over. The Panthers entered Friday having played only three home games this season, the fewest in the NHL. More than half the league had logged at least seven home games going into the day.

items.body: Matt Pavelich, enshrined in the Hockey Hall of Fame in 1987 in the Referee/Linespersons category, died on Friday at age 92. His death was reported on social media by his son, Mark, who said that Pavelich was “surrounded by the people who loved him” at the end. The first linesman inducted into the Hall of Fame, the category expanded in 1987 to include linesmen along with referees, Pavelich officiated in the NHL for 23 seasons, his body of work totaling 1,727 regular-season games as a linesman and 14 more as a referee, another 245 games worked in the Stanley Cup Playoffs. Born March 12, 1934 in Parkhill, Ontario, Pavelich worked the 1957 and 1958 Stanley Cup Finals, and then 19 consecutive Finals between 1961-79 for a total of 56 Cup Final games. Famously, Pavelich and late Montreal Canadiens goalie Ken Dryden worked the final games of their careers on May 21, 1979, Game 5 of the Stanley Cup Final. The Canadiens’ 4-1 victory against the New York Rangers gave Montreal the 22nd of its 24 championships to date. Matt Pavelich in an undated portrait, early in his career, and in a photo with the Hall of Fame’s Class of 1987: Bob Clarke, John Ziegler and Eddie Giacomin from left in the back row, Pavelich and Jacques Laperriere in the front. Pavelich and Dryden were firmly connected by the final siren of that game, and by a rolling puck that was headed toward the glove of the 1983 Hall of Fame-bound goalie as the celebrations began in the Forum. This was the sixth Stanley Cup title for Dryden in his seven full Canadiens seasons, with him having won his first after just six regular-season games in 1970-71. items.summary: Connor Hellebuyck stopped 19 shots, Arseny Gritsyuk and Jack Hughes each scored twice and the New Jersey Devils beat the Vegas Golden Knights 5-2 on Friday.
items.body: LAS VEGAS — Connor Hellebuyck stopped 19 shots, Arseny Gritsyuk and Jack Hughes each scored twice and the New Jersey Devils beat the Vegas Golden Knights 5-2 on Friday. Hellebuyck, who spent his first 11 seasons in the NHL with the Winnipeg Jets, had his second win since the Devils acquired him Oct. 23 . The three-time Vezina Trophy also was in goal Tuesday night in Dallas in a 5-1 win. Gritsyuk has scored at least a goal in six of the last eight games and has 10 points during the stretch. Luke Hughes also scored for New Jersey. The Devils improved to 10-1-0 when the Hughes brothers score in the same game. Mark Stone and Ivan Barbashev scored for the Golden Knights, and Adin Hill stopped 26 shots. Luke Hughes got things going early in the first when he rifled a one-timer from the top of the left circle past Hill. Stone tied it when he deflected Mitch Marner’s blast from the point past Hellebuyck. Barbashev gave the Knights a 2-1 lead moments later when he tapped Marner’s pass home after a picture-perfect cross-crease pass. The lead didn’t last one minute, as Gritsyuk took advantage of a turnover and sniped Hill top shelf from the left circle. Jack Hughes put New Jersey back in front when he stole the puck from Jack Eichel in the neutral zone, then passed it to himself through Stone’s legs before beating Hill. Gritsyuk scored his second goal by backhanding his rebound after Hill blocked his first attempt.

Challenge Initiated By: Florida
Type of Challenge: Puck Out of Play
Result: Call on the ice is upheld

items.body: Explanation: The play on the ice was challenged under Rule 38 – Coach’s Challenge. Rule 38.1 states, “In all Coach’s Challenge situations, the original call on the ice will be overturned if, and only if, a conclusive and irrefutable determination can be made on the basis of video evidence that the original call on the ice was clearly not correct. If a review is not conclusive and/or there is any doubt whatsoever as to whether the call on the ice was correct, the original call on the ice will be confirmed.” After a thorough examination of all available replays, there was no conclusive evidence that the puck shot by Florida’s Dmitry Kulikov at 12:03 (7:57 elapsed time) was deflected before going out of play . Therefore, the call on the ice stands. The decision was made in accordance with Rule 38.2 (d) which states, in part, that a team may request a Coach’s Challenge “When a minor penalty for delaying the game has been assessed under Rule 63.2 (iii) for shooting or batting the puck out of play from the defending zone. This will only apply to delay of game penalties when the shot/batted puck is determined to have subsequently deflected off a player, stick, glass or boards, etc., and not a judgment call.” Therefore, an additional minor penalty was assessed to Florida (in addition to the existing delay of game penalty).

items.title: Senators’ Hodgson suspended two games for boarding Kings’ Clarke
items.body: Hayden Hodgson will be watching the next two games from the press box. The Ottawa Senators forward has been suspended for two games for boarding, the NHL's Department of Player Safety announced Friday. The punishment comes after Hodgson received a game misconduct and major penalty for boarding Los Angeles Kings defenceman Brandt Clarke on Thursday night. Hodgson took a run at Clarke, charging in at 21 m.p.h., according to the game broadcast. Clarke was just below the goal line when he was driven into the boards. The hit caused a brief scrum, and the Kings' Erik Haula received a two-minute penalty for roughing Hodgson. Clarke was ruled out for the rest of the game for what the Kings called an upper-body injury. The play with 8:45 left in the second period came shortly after the Kings scored three goals in 4:03 to take a 4-1 lead and chase goalie Jonas Johansson. Hodgson has played in only 24 NHL games over five seasons, but including Thursday, has amassed 51 minutes in penalties. Hodgson was fined $2,018, the maximum allowed under the terms of the collective bargaining agreement, in October 2025 for boarding Montreal's Alex Newhook in a pre-season game. He has a long history of suspensions — 20 games worth — in the American Hockey League for elbowing and other offences over the past five seasons. He’ll forfeit $8,763 in salary as a result of the suspension. He'll miss games Saturday at San Jose and Sunday at Anaheim. He's eligible to return Wednesday at Buffalo. items.body: Register Login Ducks Assign Nikita Klepov To OHL By Brennan McClain | at October 30, 2026 3:32 pm According to a team announcement , the Anaheim Ducks have returned forward Nikita Klepov to the OHL’s Saginaw Spirit. Klepov will remain with the Spirit through the end of the 2026-27 campaign and attempt to crack Anaheim’s roster next season. Because he didn’t reach the 10-game mark, or even come close, the Ducks can now slide Klepov’s entry-level contract despite him making his NHL debut. Klepov finishes his first four NHL contests going scoreless with a -2 rating, averaging 13:03 of ice time per game. On the one hand, it’s a smart move by Anaheim; even though Klepov had five more games of eligibility, the recent 15th overall pick should get more playing time. Now, Klepov can pick up where he left off with Saginaw. He scored 37 goals and 97 points in 67 games for the Spirit last season. Unfortunately for Saginaw, the Kitchener Rangers swept them in the 2026 OHL Playoffs conference quarterfinals. On the other hand, the Ducks may have missed the mark by signing Klepov to his entry-level contract so early. Before signing his first professional contract, Klepov was committed to play at Michigan State University for the 2026-27 campaign. However, since he signed a professional deal, he was no longer eligible for the NCAA. Instead, Klepov returns to a level he has already dominated after making four NHL appearances. If the Ducks weren’t planning to give him more opportunity, it would have been wiser to have him remain without a contract so he could play for the Spartans.

items.body: Josh Manson is expected to miss eight weeks for the Colorado Avalanche because of an ankle injury, coach Jared Bednar said Friday. The defenseman left a 5-2 win against the New Jersey Devils on Wednesday at 15:19 of the first period after falling awkwardly after a missed body check and did not return. Manson has four points (one goal, three assists) in 13 games this season. He leads the Avalanche in hits (28) and is third in blocked shots (17). He is in his sixth season with the Avalanche and won the Stanley Cup with them in 2022. "It's a kind of (an) irreplaceable loss," Colorado defenseman Brett Kulak said. Like I think it could have been a lot worse than it was." With Manson out of the lineup, Noah Juulsen is expected to be a regular in the lineup. He has one assist in eight games this season and is averaging 10:38 of ice time per game. "I love his attitude. He wants to do anything he can to help," Bednar said. "He's a real positive guy, and he's played great for us. So yeah, we're going to need him, obviously, with 'Mans' being out for eight weeks. items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Colorado Avalanche head coach Jared Bednar announced on Friday that defenseman Josh Manson is going to about miss eight weeks due to an ankle injury. The injury occurred late in the first period of Wednesday’s 5-2 win over the New Jersey Devils after taking a weird hit. He struggled to get off the ice and had to be helped down the tunnel, and did not return to the game after that. The Avalanche confirmed his departure at the start of the third period. Manson’s current timeline for return has him set to return after the holiday break, which will mean the Avalanche will be without him for at least 20 games barring a quicker recovery than expected. The Avalanche also haven’t announced a stint on injured reserve for Manson yet, but it wouldn’t be surprising if that happens sometime down the road. Manson joins Zachary L’Heureux on the Avalanche’s injury list, with L’Heureux out on a day-to-day basis with a lower-body injury. Manson has had a solid start to the season with one goal and three assists for four points in 13 games . That puts him on pace for his usual production in the 20-30 point range. While no lineup has been confirmed for Saturday’s game against the Calgary Flames , Noah Juulsen is the only other defenseman on the Avalanche roster who didn’t play on Wednesday, and will likely draw into the lineup on the third pairing. items.title: Mike Babcock’s Oilers overhaul paying off through structure, accountability
items.summary: Suddenly, the Oilers can win games with their defensive structure. And like the guy or not, there is a two-word answer for all of it: Mike Babcock. Sportsnet’s Mark Spector has more.
items.body: EAST MEADOW, N.Y. — Don’t look now, but the Edmonton Oilers lead the National Hockey League in rush chances against, and rank 25th in rush chances for. Connor McDavid played just 18:50 last game. Tristan Jarry had a shutout. And like the guy or not, there is a two-word answer for all of it: Mike Babcock. “You're getting called out on whatever you're not doing right to help the team win,” Leon Draisaitl said on Friday. That is exactly what McDavid was talking about back in June, when he, Zach Hyman and Draisaitl took a very active role in the Babcock hire. “It's time to have that happen in Edmonton,” McDavid said that day. “I’m excited about that challenge to be pushed by a coach, because it's been a really long time in Edmonton.” Today, the puck-possession Oilers rank second in the NHL in dump-in rate. They also rank second in puck battles won. “It's a simple game and (it is) determined by effort,” Babcock explained. “But if you have effort and you don't have structure, you're not playing together. You've got to arrive as five everywhere; you've got to play together. And the more you know what the other person's doing, the more space there is for all of you.” It is explicit what a player must do to remain a part of this transition from that free-wheeling, firewagon team that got odd-manned rushed right out of the playoffs by the Anaheim Ducks last spring. “It's very clear when (Babcock) talks, guys listen,” said veteran Mattias Ekholm. “If I'd say one thing tactically or even structurally that he does really well, he does eliminate those grey areas.” The first casualty of a new coach with new expectations? items.title: Six key takeaways from the first month of the NHL season
items.summary: What have we learned through the first month of the NHL season? We take a look around the league at some takeaways as the calendar gets set to flip to November.
items.body: One full month of NHL action is behind us. With more than five months of regular-season play still ahead of us, there is still so much that can happen. What we think we may know about the season less than 20 per cent of the way in could change drastically by April — or, some early signs could stick and become season-long narratives. At this one-month touchpoint, we take a look around the league at some key early takeaways: At least three teams from the Atlantic — and maybe four! — will finish with crushing disappointment We knew this would be a competitive division, but this start has been wild. Everybody in the Atlantic has a points percentage over .500 — Toronto currently ranks last with a .533 points percentage and the Maple Leafs have felt competitive with a 7-6-2 record. Only two teams — Detroit (minus-1) and Buffalo (minus-7) — have a negative goal differential. All of these teams have playoff expectations — even Detroit, with all the drama around Dylan Larkin and Simon Edvinsson, has a 10-year playoff drought it is trying to squash this season. We already see that at least three teams will head into the summer with some very difficult questions about firings and roster changes to answer — only because of the division they're in. items.body: Register Login Assessing Elias Pettersson’s Potential Trade Value By Josh Cybulski | at October 30, 2026 1:00 pm It might seem crazy, but we are moving into a world where Vancouver Canucks forward Elias Pettersson might have meaningful trade value. Not just a bit of value, but potentially a decent amount if he keeps producing at the rate he has through 14 games this year. So far this year, the 27-year-old has notched four goals and 11 assists and is starting to look more like the player who signed an eight-year, $92.8MM contract extension in March 2024. That deal, which included $47MM in signing bonuses, looked unmovable and buyout-proof just 12 months ago, but with his hot start and an exploding salary cap, Pettersson could become a bit of a bargain. Now, 14 games at a point-per-game pace doesn’t automatically make Pettersson a Hart Trophy contender or even a top 25 scorer in the NHL. But if he can return to a 70+ point pace, he and his contract could have value in the new NHL economy, where some players are getting deals north of $20MM annually. If it seems crazy, that’s because it is. This past summer rewrote the NHL salary landscape, and it appears player salaries could keep trending upward. However, that’s not certain, which could create urgency for the Canucks to trade Pettersson if/when he has value. Yet teams could remain hesitant to make the move for Pettersson given his track record over the last few years. The Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) ruled on Friday that Russia must be eligible to return to ice hockey world championships, and hockey's governing bodies have responded. The ruling has the chance to impact Russian participation in five upcoming international events, with the upcoming IIHF World Junior Championships being first to commence on Dec. 26 in Edmonton and Red Deer, Alta. later this year. The IIHF responded to the news Friday morning, expressing its "disappointment with the decision." However, the IIHF will ultimately act in accordance with the CAS's ruling. While the Ukrainian hockey federation stated it respects the authority and status of the CAS, they align with the IIHF in its disagreement. items.title: Flames goaltender Devin Cooley week-to-week with lower-body injury
items.summary: The Calgary Flames will be without Devin Cooley for a while.
items.body: The team placed the goaltender on injured reserve Friday with a lower-body injury after he was forced to exit Wednesday's game against the Edmonton Oilers. Head coach Ryan Huska told reporters that Cooley will be week-to-week. Oilers forward Colton Dach crashed into Cooley with 12 seconds remaining in the opening 20 minutes and received a two-minute penalty for goaltender interference. Cooley remained in for the final 12 seconds but was not on the bench to start the second. He was then ruled out for the remainder of the game with a lower-body injury, the team announced. The 29-year-old had allowed just six goals on 133 shots over his previous four games entering Wednesday's game, good for a .955 save percentage. With Cooley out, Dustin Wolf is set to start the Flames' game against the Seattle Kraken Friday night (Sportsnet West, Sportsnet+, 8 p.m. ET / 6 p.m. MT). It will mark his first start since Oct. 15. items.body: Add to Preferred Sources The NHL Department of Player Safety announced on Friday that Ottawa Senators winger Hayden Hodgson will have a hearing for boarding and charging Los Angeles Kings defenseman Brandt Clarke during the Sens’ 6-5 overtime loss on Thursday. The infraction occurred midway during the second period of the game. As the Senators were dumping the puck into the Kings’ zone on an offensive rush, Clarke skated towards the boards in an attempt to make a play on the puck and regain possession. In doing so, he turned towards the boards, which opened the door for Hodgson to hit him from behind. In addition to the boarding, Hodgson also began to build up momentum for the hit from the top of the faceoff circle, a clear charging infraction on the play. As a result of the hit, Hodgson received a five-minute major penalty for boarding, as well as a 10-minute misconduct, and was ejected from the game. Kings’ center Erik Haula immediately responded to the hit and stuck up for Clarke by going after Hodgson, which resulted in a two-minute minor penalty for the Kings as well. Los Angeles also burned Hodgson and the Senators on the ensuing power play, as Artemi Panarin scored to give them a 5-1 lead, one they would blow in the third period before ultimately winning the game in overtime. The first tournament the ruling affects is the world junior championship, starting Dec. 26 in Edmonton and Red Deer, Alta. The ruling is a major win for Russia against efforts to bar it from international sports due to the war in Ukraine. Russian President Vladimir Putin is a noted hockey fan who has previously played exhibition games with former stars. CAS overturned IIHF decisions which excluded Russia from events in the 2026-27 season including the men’s and women’s world championships. Russia also missed the Olympics tournaments this year. Russia's return throws into uncertainty how the men's world championship will work next year in Germany, given that Ukraine has also qualified. In a brief statement, CAS cited a lack of sufficient evidence to support the IIHF’s security concerns. CAS said its ruling did not address issues such as whether Russia should be required to play without national symbols as a team of neutral athletes, as in some other Olympic sports, or other “organizational consequences.” The IIHF expressed disappointment with the ruling and said it “maintains that its decisions were necessary to protect the safety and security of all participants and safeguard the integrity of its competitions." “While the IIHF respects the authority of CAS and will act in accordance with its ruling, the outcome does not remove the concerns that informed its assessments.” Russian Sports Minister Mikhail Degtyaryov wrote on the Telegram social media app that CAS “recognized the demands of the Russian Hockey Federation on key points as justified.” The ruling is an immediate ch

items.summary: The Canucks were following their first win in 11 games with their best game of the season. Then, suddenly, they weren’t.
items.body: The Vancouver Canucks were following their first win in 11 games with their best game of the National Hockey League season. Then, suddenly, they weren’t. Until Jonathan Lekkerimaki followed a risky neutral-zone turnover with his second interference penalty of the game at 6:59 of the third period, the Canucks looked almost comfortable carrying a two-goal lead over the San Jose Sharks. But Will Smith’s power-play goal sparked a three-goal outburst in just over three minutes as the Sharks exploded to beat the Vancouver Canucks 3-2 in San Jose. The Canucks pushed for a late tying goal, generating a couple of outstanding scoring chances while skating six-on-four and six-on-five, but were unable to salvage anything in the standings from a game in which they looked for 47 minutes as composed and structured as they have been this season. The loss followed Vancouver’s improbable 6-5 overtime road win Tuesday against the Anaheim Ducks. The Canucks were far sounder against Macklin Celebrini’s team in San Jose, plugging passing lanes, backchecking consistently and generally keeping the speedy Sharks in front of them after a couple of glaring breakdowns in the opening five minutes. Analytics site Natural Stat Trick had the Canucks better by a goal at five-on-five, and ahead 7-4 on high-danger scoring chances. items.body: LOS ANGELES — Quinton Byfield scored at 3:37 of overtime and the Los Angeles Kings beat the Ottawa Senators 6-5 on Thursday night after blowing a four-goal lead in the third period. Byfield beat goalie Samuel Ersson with a snap shot from the high slot, with Drew Doughty picking up his third assist of the night on the play. Erik Haula tied it for Los Angeles on a first-period power play and Trevor Moore, Mikey Anderson, Joel Armia and Artemi Panarin scored in the second to make it 5-1. Panarin capped the run on a power play after Ottawa's Hayden Hodgson was tossed for boarding defenseman Brandt Clarke. Clarke missed the rest of the game because of an upper-body injury. Ottawa roared back in the third, with Shane Pinto tying it at 5 with 1:40 left and Ersson off for an extra attacker. Dylan Cozens scored twice in the period and Drake Batherson also connected. Cozens and Batherson struck in a 33-second span, and Cozens cut it to a goal with 7:26 remaining. Tyler Kleven opened the scoring for Ottawa in the first period. Jonas Johansson stopped 12 of 16 shots before giving way to Ersson in the second. Ersson made 20 saves on 22 shots.

items.title: ‘It meant a little more’: Seider on Red Wings’ win after Larkin suspension
items.summary: Larkin was suspended by the Red Wings on Thursday after he announced he would sit out until he was traded.
items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: Brian Bradshaw Sevald-Imagn Images Moritz Seider didn’t shy away from the importance of the Detroit Red Wings’ 4-1 win against the Chicago Blackhawks Thursday night, just hours after the franchise suspended former captain Dylan Larkin without pay . “It meant a little more,” Seider, who finished the night with an assist and 18:49 of ice time, told reporters after the game. “I think it came down to that this is our squad and we got a really good group in here.” The Red Wings suspended Larkin on Thursday after he announced through his agent he would no longer play for the team and sit out until he was traded. “It’s tough, but in the end, you just want him to be happy. If that’s not here, hopefully it’s somewhere else,” Seider said. “It’s kind of hard to put that player aspect aside and just see it as a friend, but ultimately, that’s my goal: him being happy and us being competitive.” The 25-year-old defenseman said he had no indication that Larkin was no longer willing to play for the team he captained for nearly six years. “We welcomed him with open arms, we were open-minded and didn’t let a situation like in Winnipeg happen,” a reference to Connor Hellebuyck’s trade request from the Winnipeg Jets that ended with him being traded to the New Jersey Devils earlier this week. “I think that’s a big credit to this locker room, too,” he added. “Now you just want to move on, figure some things out, and now some other guys will step up.” Seider also said he was hopeful the Red Wings get a good return in a potential Larkin trade. “You want this to be a proud organization where players want to be here, and want to be here long term. Hopefully, we can set a great example during the course of the year.”

items.body: SAN JOSE, Calif. — Will Smith scored twice, including the tying goal just 11 seconds before Mason Marchment’s go-ahead goal, and the San Jose Sharks rallied from a two-goal deficit to beat the Vancouver Canucks 3-2 on Thursday night. Marchment had a goal and an assist, while Macklin Celebrini recorded his 16th point of the season with an assist. Yaroslav Askarov made 23 saves for San Jose. Smith scored his first goal at 8:00 of the third period on a power play to get the Sharks on the board. San Jose had gone 0 for 4 on the power play before Smith’s goal. Smith tied the game with his second goal at 10:39, with Celebrini recording the assist. Marchment then gave the Sharks their first lead at 10:50. Drew O’Connor and Liam Ohgren scored for Vancouver, while Elias Pettersson and Filip Hronek had an assist. Leevi Merilainen stopped 21 shots for the Canucks. O’Connor opened the scoring at 13:21 of the first period for his second goal of the season, scoring on a rebound with an assist from Pettersson. San Jose defenseman Dmitry Orlov tried to clear the puck but was stripped, leading to the goal. Ohgren extended Vancouver’s lead to 2-0 at 18:56 of the second period with his fourth goal of the season. The Canucks have lost 11 of their last 12 games, having snapped a 10-game losing streak with their previous win. Sharks fans booed as Vancouver took its two-goal lead into the second intermission.

Burakovsky fell to the ice after protecting the puck along the boards for an extended period of time, and was slow to get up. Ottawa is already missing forwards William Eklund and Warren Foegele due to injury. Burakovsky, 31, was scoreless in seven games coming into Thursday. The Senators acquired Burakovsky from the Chicago Blackhawks this past offseason in exchange for a sixth-round pick in the 2027 NHL Entry Draft. Last season with Chicago, he notched 11 goals and 22 assists for 33 points in 75 games. An undrafted 6’2″ winger from Windsor, Ont., Hodgson has spent the majority of his professional career to date in the AHL and ECHL. Thursday’s game was the 24th of his NHL career, and his 17th with the Senators. Hodgson has primarily served as an enforcer across his time with the AHL’s Lehigh Valley Phantoms, Ontario Reign, and Belleville Senators. He amassed 134 penalty minutes but just 11 points in 47 games with Belleville during the 2025-26 AHL regular season; he was also suspended multiple times for illegal hits and other aggressive on-ice behavior. Perhaps it leads to more homework or a different perspective the next time you see that player. If your opinion remains unchanged, that's fine. We still have done our job. items.title: Seider reacts to Larkin leaving Red Wings: ‘Turn the page’
items.summary: Moritz Seider is looking ahead as his former captain waits at home for a trade.
items.body: Moritz Seider is looking ahead as his former captain waits at home for a trade. The Detroit Red Wings ' top defenceman said, "It's good to put it in the past and turn the page," after Dylan Larkin left the team and was suspended without pay on Thursday. "Whoever we get, whatever pick we get, we'll have players that are happy to be here," Seider said after the Red Wings beat the Chicago Blackhawks 4-1. "We just have to make sure we get them ready to be part of our team." Larkin requested a trade out of Detroit in the spring but had been playing while awaiting a deal, even scoring a big goal late in a win over the Oilers on Monday. But on Thursday, interim general manager Shawn Horcoff announced that Larkin "has informed us that he will no longer play for the Detroit Red Wings," so the team suspended the veteran centre as they weigh offers. The news came hours before the Red Wings hosted former teammate Patrick Kane and the rival Chicago Blackhawks in a game broadcast on ESPN, but after a slow start, Detroit rallied to win thanks to a hat trick from newcomer Viktor Arvidsson to improve to 6-4-3 on the season. "Obviously it meant a little more," Seider said of winning after the drama of the day. "I think it came down to this is our squad and we have a really good group in here." Seider, who is likely to succeed Larkin as captain, said he wishes nothing but the best to his now-former teammate. "Obviously it's tough but in the end you want him to be happy and if that's not here hopefully it's somewhere else," Seider said. "It's kinda hard to put that player aspect aside and just see it as a friend, but ultimately that's my goal... Nevertheless, we still have a hell of a group in here."

items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: Mandatory Credit: Wendell Cruz-Imagn Images The New York Islanders announced that defenseman Ryan Pulock will not return to Thursday’s game against the Minnesota Wild due to an upper-body injury. Pulock sustained the injury early in the first period of the game, only playing in two shifts before he exited the match. It’s unclear what exactly caused the injury, but the most likely incident was when he was battling along the boards with Yakov Trenin, as he skated gingerly after the fact. He went to the dressing room after and did not return, with the team confirming his absence at the start of the second period. Pulock played just 51 seconds of ice time in those two shifts, with only a hit taken on his stat line before exiting the game. The Islanders were already down 1-0 at the time of his early departure. There’s currently no other updates on Pulock, including the severity of the injury and how much time he’s expected to miss. Islanders head coach Pete DeBoer might give an update after the game, but since the Isles are at the end of a three-game road trip before returning home, it’s likely that a more specific update isn’t provided until a practice or morning skate on Long Island. items.title: Jets rally but fall to Lightning for seventh straight loss
items.body: TAMPA, Fla. — Pontus Holmberg set a career high with four points on a goal and three assists, Brandon Hagel and Anthony Cirelli each had a goal and two assists, and the Tampa Bay Lightning remain unbeaten at home with a 6-4 victory over the Winnipeg Jets on Thursday night. Brayden Point, John Carlson and Conor Geekie all scored for Tampa Bay. Andrei Vasilevskiy stopped 17 shots. The Lightning improved to 6-0 at home to tie a franchise record to start a season. Neil Pionk, playing his 600th game, scored twice. Kyle Connor and Dylan Samberg also scored for the Jets and Mark Scheifele had three assists. Stuart Skinner allowed five goals on 21 shots before being replaced by Nico Daws to start the third period. Daws finished with nine saves in his Winnipeg debut. Winnipeg is winless (0-5-2) in the past seven games, including three consecutive regulation losses since trading goaltender Connor Hellebuyck to New Jersey. After Point and Pionk traded goals in the first period, Tampa Bay pulled away in the second period with four goals, including three in the final 4:04. Geekie backhanded in a pass from Dominic James at 9:43 before Cirelli scored a power-play goal at 15:56, getting his stick on a cross-crease pass from Holmberg. Carlson made it 4-1 at 18:07 as he one-timed Holmberg's pass from the left faceoff dot. Hagel finished off the period with a tap-in from Cirelli at the back post with 56 seconds left in the period. Winnipeg scored two goals less than two minutes apart in the third to cut into the lead. Perfetti fed Samberg for a one-handed redirect at 7:00 while Pionk scored his second at 8:50, with Dawson Mercer registering his first point with the Jets on the play. items.body: The Nashville Predators inducted their former head coach and general manager into the Golden Hall before the team’s game against the Washington Capitals at Bridgestone Arena. Predators owner Bill Haslam, former general manager David Poile and team CEO Sean Henry joined Trotz on the ice for the ceremony. A special tribute video of Trotz’s career with Nashville aired on the arena video board. After the video, Poile presented the golden jacket to Trotz as “Barry! Barry!” chants rang from the crowd. “Thank you so much, thank you,” Trotz said. “I’ve been blessed to work with three wonderful organizations and two are here tonight. He coached Ovechkin and the Capitals from 2014-2018, leading them to their first Stanley Cup title in 2018. Ovechkin and Tom Wilson gifted their former coach a custom bottle of wine. items.body: Register Login Hurricanes’ Taylor Hall Out Day-To-Day By Gabriel Foley | at October 29, 2026 7:10 pm Taylor Hall has fallen back out of the Carolina Hurricanes lineup with a day-to-day injury. The 34 year old sustained a new injury in Tuesday’s practice, unrelated to his upper-body injury sustained on October 13th, per ESPN’s Emily Kaplan . Hall has not played since his initial injury, though he was activated off of injured reserve on Monday . He went on to miss Tuesday’s game against the Boston Bruins, marking six consecutive absences for Hall. The Hurricanes offense is inevitably shorthanded without Hall in the lineup. His absence keeps Carolina from rolling out the trio of Hall, Logan Stankoven , and Jackson Blake – a unit that has outscored opponents 38-to-26 dating back to last season. They won the scoring battle three-to-one through the first eight games of this season. Individually, Hall has racked up five points in eight appearances. Half of that scoring came from back-to-back two-point performances on October 6th and 8th. The Hurricanes combined for 13 goals between those two games. Carolina has continued to find success despite Hall’s absence. They lead the NHL with a 10-2-2 record and rank third in scoring with 3.79 goals-per-game. Stankoven and Blake have been joined by Nikolaj Ehlers , forming a line that has four goals-for and no goals-against. Hall’s absence has also opened an opportunity for Nicolas Deslauriers , who should stick on the fourth-line until the former Hart Trophy winner is back to full health. items.body: Add to Preferred Sources The Detroit Red Wings announced on Thursday that they have suspended center Dylan Larkin without pay. The decision comes in the wake of Larkin not attending team practice on Wednesday. He had initially been announced as out for Thursday’s game against the Chicago Blackhawks , but then Larkin announced he’d be sitting out until he was traded through his agent, Pat Brisson. items.title: PWHL increases minimum salary and roster size for 2026-27
items.summary: The PWHL is increasing the minimum pay for players, while also taking away the “reserve player” status from team roster builds.
items.body: Add to Preferred Sources The PWHL is increasing the minimum player salary from around $38,000 to $42,000 for the 2026-27 season and will raise it to $52,500 by the 2030-31 season, the league and the PWHL Players Association announced Thursday. The increased salaries headline a list of sweeping changes to pay and roster construction, including teams increasing to 24-player rosters for the upcoming campaign and abolishing the league’s “reserve player” status, which had players in full-commitment but only making $15,000 as a full-season stipend. “As the PWHL expands from eight to 12 teams, these changes reflect our shared commitment to creating more opportunities for players, strengthening the economic foundation of professional women’s hockey and supporting the league’s long-term growth,” the joint statement said. “The PWHL and PWHLPA remain committed to working collaboratively to advance player opportunities, compensation, and the continued growth of professional women’s hockey.” With the increase in roster sizes, 288 players will be under contract for the 2026-27 season across the league’s dozen teams, now split into two conferences of six for the first time. At the same time, teams can use a One-Game Standard Player Agreement mechanism to sign replacements in case of injuries or other hardships that hit the roster. While the season is not set to get underway until Dec. 5, competitive hockey has already dropped the puck, with pre-tournament international games in the lead-up to the first edition of the rescheduled fall IIHF Women’s World Championship , set to take place in Denmark from Nov. 6-16 as a precursor to the professional season in North America. By Josh Cybulski | at October 29, 2026 3:10 pm Pittsburgh Penguins general manager Kyle Dubas took a page from the Tampa Bay Rays’ playbook by signing forward Ville Koivunen to an eight-year, $32MM extension this past summer . As the Rays have done for years, Dubas locked up an unproven player with a big extension at a surprising price. It’s worked for the Rays for decades, but the NHL rarely does it, and Dubas could pioneer it with Koivunen. However, if it doesn’t work, Dubas will have a pricey gamble on his hands. But if it does, will it change how other GMs operate? It will be a long time before we know whether his deal will give Pittsburgh value, and two weeks ago it looked like a disaster. But after a couple of solid games, including an overtime winner against Nashville on Saturday night, Koivunen is starting to show some upside. Pittsburgh’s signing of Koivunen was peculiar for several reasons, including the timing, as it came after a relatively quiet summer in which Dubas swung and missed on nearly every trade and free-agent target. The signing almost felt like a panic reaction from Dubas, who may have realized he couldn’t acquire young top-six talent and pivoted to locking in a player with top-six potential. Pundits universally panned the signing and largely mocked it , unable to believe Pittsburgh would lock up a player to a max-term deal who had just two goals and five assists in 39 NHL games last season. Helenius, 20, sustained the injury during Buffalo’s 2-0 win over the San Jose Sharks on Tuesday evening. The Sabres still have two games remaining on their current road trip, but Helenius is heading back to Buffalo early to undergo further evaluation. Through 11 games with the Sabres this season, Helenius has one goal and three points. The 5-foot-11 forward is currently in the second season of his three-year, entry-level NHL contract. With Helenius slated to miss time with his injury, the Sabres announced that forward Sam Carrick is expected to be activated off the injured reserve list and could return to the lineup in Thursday’s game against the Anaheim Ducks . items.body: Register Login Snapshots: Shabanov, Lardis, 2027 Draft By Ethan Hetu | at October 29, 2026 2:33 pm While it’s still very early in the 2026-27 season, it’s not too early to begin looking at players who may be setting themselves up to earn a big pay raise in the summer. With the salary cap rising at a steep rate, promising individual performances can have even more weight as teams look to identify and pay players before those players can realize the full extent of their value on the open market. The Anaheim Ducks’ decision to pay Tristan Luneau , with less than 30 NHL games to his name, a $7.2MM AAV on a long-term contract extension serves as an illustration of this principle in action. One player who is lining himself up to earn a substantial pay raise is Minnesota Wild winger Max Shabanov . The 26-year-old former KHL star endured a difficult NHL rookie season with the New York Islanders in 2025-26, and New York ultimately non-tendered him after he scored just 18 points in 44 games. The Wild inked Shabanov to a one-year, $1.6MM deal, and he’ll be an RFA with arbitration rights over the summer. His early-season form suggests a major pay raise could be in store, as he’s found himself a regular role on Minnesota’s top power play unit and has produced nine points in his first 13 games with the Wild.
